summary: Weekly POC sync to review first-week pilot results, confirm onboarding progress (VPC access, test accounts), and agree next tuning steps. Main findings: initial latency is acceptable for dev traffic but 95/99p needs improvement; batching and KV cache expected to reduce cost/latency; security docs requested and SSO/SAML questions outstanding.
topics: Tuning plan: batching, KV cache, quantization suggestions
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey folks, good morning, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Alex from Redwood, Priya our SE, and Samir from success.
[00:10] John Carter: Hi, John here — CTO. Maria, Ethan, Leah with me.
[00:16] Alex Kim: Great. Agenda is bench results, access & onboarding, and tuning steps. We'll keep to 45.
[00:30] Priya Nair: Jumping in on results — we ran the initial throughput tests last night, these are the numbers. The average p50 latency per request was about 180 ms with batching=1, token throughput around 220 tps on the dedicated instance we spun up. There were a couple of spikes at the 99th at ~880 ms.
[00:50] Maria Sanchez: Sorry can I interrupt — 880 ms at 99p, is that with KV cache on?
[00:55] Priya Nair: No, this was baseline without KV caching. We ran one KV test as well — that brought 95p down to mid-200s and 99p to about 420 ms. There's some noise though because of the long tail when the seq length was 1024 for a couple of requests.
[01:15] Leah Park: Did you do quantized model runs? We saw lower memory but curious on perf.
[01:20] Priya Nair: We did a q4 run — memory dropped by ~40% and cost per token down as expected, but latency was slightly higher on some kernels. We're recommending q4 for throughput-heavy batch jobs, but q8 or fp16 for low-latency inference.
[01:35] John Carter: Ok, makes sense. Our main concern is user-facing latency — we target 300ms median and <500ms 95th ideally.
[01:45] Alex Kim: Right. With batching and KV cache we can likely meet 95p <500ms for many of your shorter prompts. For the longer seqs (1k tokens) you may need model-shortening or offloading longer context to background.
[02:00] Ethan Wu: On the access side — we tried the test account but can't reach the endpoint from our dev subnet. I'm assuming VPC peering isn't configured yet.
[02:08] Alex Kim: Correct, we have not seen the VPC peering request. Ethan, can you share the CIDR and I can get infra to kick the peering?
[02:15] Ethan Wu: I'll send the CIDR after this call. Also question on IP allowlist — do you support static egress IPs?
[02:22] Samir Patel: We can provide a set of egress IPs for Dedicated and Private installs; for hosted there's a managed pool but for Dedicated we'll pin.
[02:30] Maria Sanchez: Security: we need SOC 2 evidence and SAML SSO flow. Who owns that from Redwood?
[02:36] Alex Kim: Samir on success will send SOC 2 and our security pack. For SAML, Priya can help with the SSO flow and we'll provide SAML metadata.
[02:45] Samir Patel: I'll attach the SOC 2 cert, network diagrams, and the standard penetration test summary to the Confluence link after.
[02:52] John Carter: Perfect. On cost — the initial numbers in the spreadsheet look higher than we expected. Any quick wins?
[02:58] Priya Nair: Yes — toggling batching from 1 to 4 reduced token compute by about 25% in our test and improved throughput. KV prefix caching reduces repeated token costs for multi-turn chat. Also model selection: e.g., switching to a quantized mid-size model reduced cost ~35% with modest quality diff.
[03:20] Leah Park: Are there known regressions when quantizing? Sometimes hallucinations spike.
[03:25] Priya Nair: Good question — we do evaluation harnesses; we'll tie the evals to your prompt set. For the pilot we ran a small eval and saw a slight drop in exact-match on entity extraction, but still within your threshold as discussed earlier.
[03:40] Alex Kim: Quick housekeeping — shared artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet (https://drive.redwood/HealthOptimize-pilot-bench.xlsx), security pack (https://redwood.docs/security/HO-pkg), and sample config repo link.
[03:52] John Carter: Thanks. On the peering timeline — we need to test with realistic traffic early next week.
[03:58] Ethan Wu: We'll aim to send creds and CIDR by Tuesday.
[04:05] Alex Kim: Great. Priya, on tuning do you want to outline the runs we should do next?
[04:10] Priya Nair: Yes. Plan A: enable KV cache + batching=4, run 10k reqs at typical payload sizes, record p50/p95/p99 and token cost. Plan B: q4 quantized run at batching=8 for throughput tests. We'll also test fallback policy — smaller model when latency spikes.
[04:30] Maria Sanchez: For fallback, can Redwood route by latency SLO? If the primary model is busy, we want auto-fallback to a cheaper model.
[04:38] Priya Nair: Yes, smart routing supports policy-based fallback by latency and cost. There might be a small consistency difference, but it's configurable.
[04:46] John Carter: On logging and audit, do you keep request-level logs for troubleshooting? We need 90 day retention for audit.
[04:53] Samir Patel: We offer configurable retention; for Dedicated we can store logs in your S3 or forward to your SIEM. We'll document retention and access.
[05:05] Leah Park: One more on the test harness — can Redwood ingest our prompt sets and run evals automatically?
[05:10] Priya Nair: Yes, send the prompts and reference outputs; we can run the eval and return a comparison dashboard. That will show quality delta for quantized models.
[05:20] John Carter: Ok. Any blockers left?
[05:23] Ethan Wu: Blocking is VPC peering + test creds. Once we have that we can run the heavy load.
[05:30] Alex Kim: Action items recap: Alex share bench sheets & raw logs; Priya run KV+batch tests and quantized runs; Ethan send VPC info; Samir send SOC 2 packet. We'll meet again same time next week.
[05:45] Maria Sanchez: Could we also add a short deep-dive with infra next week to discuss deployment topology?
[05:50] Alex Kim: Yup, we'll schedule infra deep-dive — Priya and Samir will join.
[06:00] John Carter: Thanks everyone. Quick note — can you also include estimated pricing for Dedicated monthly commit vs hosted per-token?
[06:08] Alex Kim: I'll include a pricing comparison table in the doc I share.
[06:12] Alex Kim: Alright that's it. Thanks all.
[06:18] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (K V cache shown as "K V cash" in some auto-text), speaker labeling may be approximate.
